attack_mechanism: Debug halt and low-power controls can hold the frontend in `I_IDLE`/`E_IDLE` or delay the boundary at which a running instruction completes. `openMSP430.cpu_halt_st` controls that halt/resume path before `exec_done` is consumed by decode and fetch; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. Holding or toggling `openMSP430.cpu_halt_st` at a completion boundary can repeatedly withdraw the condition that releases the instruction state machine. The supporting RTL chain is `openMSP430.cpu_halt_st -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_first_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. Legitimate instructions cease retiring and the processor remains halted or repeatedly re-enters an incomplete execution phase.

For a ordinary execution instruction, `exec_done` is produced by the default `(e_state == E_EXEC)` completion arm. `openMSP430.frontend_0.e_first_state` sets the selected completion class, execution state, or transition into the required terminal state; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. An attacker who forces `openMSP430.frontend_0.e_first_state` away from its terminal value can keep the selected predicate false on successive `mclk` cycles. The supporting RTL chain is `openMSP430.frontend_0.e_first_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. Decode and fetch remain blocked waiting for completion, creating a persistent loss of instruction retirement.
